external_objects.notes: AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR asset Microwave_1 of objectType Microwave. Asset-database state flags: primaryProperty Moveable; secondaryProperties Receptacle, CanOpen, CanToggleOnOff, isHeatSource. AI2-THOR has no WordNet synsets, so source_taxonomy repeats the objectType as both category_id and synset_id. The asset ships inside the AI2-THOR Unity build with no per-object mesh download. tasks.name_en: Put the empty mug inside the microwave and close the door
tasks.name_ja: 空のマグカップを電子レンジに入れて扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Open the microwave, put the empty mug inside upright, and close the door.
Load the mug into the microwave and shut the door; don't start it.
電子レンジの扉を開けて空のマグカップをまっすぐ中に入れ、扉を閉めてください。加熱はしません。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (inside, with the mug kept upright) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (open the door, then close it again), over two objects in one sitting. closed and switched_off hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints, not goal changes. THOR mapping: closed(thor_object_microwave_1) <-> Microwave isOpen=false; switched_off(thor_object_microwave_1) <-> isToggled=false; inside(thor_object_mug_1, thor_object_microwave_1) <-> the Mug's parentReceptacles contains the Microwave; upright(thor_object_mug_1) is an Atlas pose predicate with no THOR state; empty(thor_object_mug_1) <-> isFilledWithLiquid=false. The goal stops before heating: switched_off is an explicit end state, so the microwave is never run. Physical collection uses an unplugged microwave; the THOR door is a scripted boolean, so a real appliance or an articulated door asset is required.

tasks.name_en: Seat a bread slice in the toaster slot and push the lever down
tasks.name_ja: 食パン1枚をトースターのスロットに差し込み、レバーを下げる
instruction_variants: Put the slice of bread into a toaster slot and press the lever down.
Load one bread slice into the toaster and switch it on.
食パンを1枚トースターの差し込み口に入れて、レバーを押し下げてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two objects and two changed predicates (slice seated, toaster on) in one sitting. THOR mapping: seated_in(thor_resource_bread_slice, thor_object_toaster_1) <-> the BreadSliced object's parentReceptacles contains the Toaster (an ObjectSpecificReceptacle); switched_on(thor_object_toaster_1) <-> Toaster isToggled=true; switched_off <-> isToggled=false. Toasting itself (isCooked) is not part of the goal. Heat framing: switched_on is observed either in simulation or on an unplugged surrogate whose lever latches mechanically; no heating element is energised in a collection cell. Many real toasters hold the carriage down with a powered electromagnet, so an unplugged unit of that design cannot show the 'on' state; the setup must declare which kind is used. The bread slice is a planning resource (BreadSliced is produced by slicing Bread in THOR, not a separate asset-database entry); a real slice or a foam surrogate may be used.

tasks.name_en: Fill a cup with water at the kitchen faucet and turn the faucet off
tasks.name_ja: キッチンの水栓でコップに水を汲み、水を止める
instruction_variants: Fill the cup with water from the kitchen tap, turn the tap off, and set the cup back on the counter.
Get a cup of water at the sink and put it on the counter without leaving the water running.
キッチンの蛇口でコップに水を入れ、蛇口を閉めてからコップを調理台に戻してください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (filled_with_water on the cup) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (faucet on, then off again), over two objects in one sitting. switched_off, upright, and the cup's counter position hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints, not goal changes. THOR mapping: filled_with_water(thor_resource_cup) <-> Cup isFilledWithLiquid=true with fillLiquid=water; switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; the cup fills in THOR when it sits under the running faucet. Physical collection defines 'filled' as water between a marked minimum and maximum line so it is observable. The cup is a planning resource: Cup exists in the asset database but is not the primary object of a part-A task.

tasks.name_en: Fill the pot with water and set it on the back burner, faucet and burner off
tasks.name_ja: 鍋に水を入れて奥のコンロに置き、水栓とコンロを切った状態にする
instruction_variants: Fill the pot with water to the line, put it on the back burner, and leave the tap and the burner off.
Get the pot ready on the back burner with water in it, but don't turn the stove on.
鍋に線まで水を入れて奥のコンロに置いてください。蛇口は閉め、コンロは点けないでください。
tasks.notes: Compound: four goal predicates over the pot, faucet, and burner in one sitting. THOR mapping: filled_with_water(thor_object_pot_1) <-> Pot isFilledWithLiquid=true, fillLiquid=water; switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; switched_off(thor_resource_stove_burner_back) <-> StoveBurner isToggled=false, which THOR drives through the paired StoveKnob; on_top_of(thor_object_pot_1, thor_resource_stove_burner_back) <-> the Pot's parentReceptacles contains the back StoveBurner. StoveBurner and StoveKnob are iTHOR room-prefab parts, not ProcTHOR asset-database entries, so they are planning resources. The burner stays off for the whole task; heating the water is out of scope. A water-filled pot is heavy, so the fill line is set from the robot's payload.

tasks.name_en: Slice the bread loaf on the cutting board
tasks.name_ja: まな板の上で食パン一斤を切り分ける
instruction_variants: Cut the loaf on the board into slices.
Slice the bread along the marked lines and leave the slices on the board.
まな板の上のパンを、印に沿ってスライスしてください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object and one goal predicate change (whole -> sliced); the loaf stays on the board. THOR mapping: sliced(thor_object_bread_1) <-> Bread isSliced=true (SliceObject with a Knife held replaces the loaf with BreadSliced pieces); whole <-> isSliced=false. The knife is an instrument, not a goal object: it starts in a guarded holder and its return there is a collection safety check at episode end, not a goal predicate. Knife safety: physical collection never uses a sharp blade near people; either the task runs in simulation only, or it uses a pre-scored surrogate loaf (for example foam segments joined by weak ties) with a blunt training knife. Slice thickness is defined by marked cut lines so 'sliced' is observable.

tasks.name_en: Throw the used-up paper towel roll into the garbage can
tasks.name_ja: 使い切ったキッチンペーパーの芯をごみ箱に捨てる
instruction_variants: Throw the empty paper towel roll in the trash.
The paper towels are finished; put the leftover roll in the garbage can.
使い終わったキッチンペーパーの芯をごみ箱に捨ててください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object and one changed predicate (on the counter -> inside the garbage can); used_up is an invariant that distinguishes the spent roll from a fresh one. THOR mapping: used_up(thor_object_paper_towel_1) <-> PaperTowelRoll isUsedUp=true; inside(thor_object_paper_towel_1, thor_resource_garbage_can) <-> the roll's parentReceptacles contains the GarbageCan. GarbageCan exists in the asset database but is not a part-A primary object, so it is a planning resource. Local rules may send a cardboard core to recycling instead; this task uses the single garbage can that THOR scenes provide.

tasks.name_en: Bring the dirty mug from the living room, rinse it, and put it away in the kitchen cabinet
tasks.name_ja: リビングの汚れたマグカップを台所ですすぎ、戸棚にしまって扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Take the dirty mug off the living-room coffee table, rinse it clean at the kitchen sink, shake the water out, and put it in the cabinet; turn off the tap and close the cabinet.
Clear the mug from the coffee table: rinse it, drain it, and store it in the kitchen cabinet with the door shut.
リビングのコーヒーテーブルにある汚れたマグカップを台所の流しですすぎ、水を切って戸棚にしまってください。蛇口を閉め、戸棚の扉も閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages in two rooms with checkpoints (mug collected from the living room; mug clean and drained with the faucet off; mug stored with the cabinet closed). THOR mapping: clean(thor_object_mug_1) <-> Mug isDirty=false; empty(thor_object_mug_1) <-> isFilledWithLiquid=false (in THOR a mug under a running faucet both cleans and fills, so draining is an explicit goal); switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; closed(thor_resource_kitchen_cabinet) <-> Cabinet isOpen=false; inside(...) <-> the Mug's parentReceptacles contains the Cabinet. Cabinet is an iTHOR room-prefab part and CoffeeTable is not a part-A primary object, so both are planning resources. Physical collection uses a water-soluble visible residue surrogate so 'clean' is checkable; drying the mug is out of scope, but no standing water may remain inside.

tasks.name_en: Fill the watering can at the kitchen tap, water the living-room plant, and put the can back
tasks.name_ja: じょうろに台所で水を汲み、リビングの植物に水をやって、じょうろを元の場所に戻す
instruction_variants: Fill the watering can at the kitchen sink, water the plant in the living room without spilling, then put the can back and make sure the tap is off.
Water the living-room houseplant using the can from its usual spot, and return the can afterwards.
台所の蛇口でじょうろに水を汲み、こぼさないようにリビングの植物に水をやってから、じょうろを元の場所に戻してください。蛇口は閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: three stages across two rooms and three destinations (fill at the kitchen sink, water in the living room, return to the home spot), with checkpoints after filling and after watering. Physical definition of watered(thor_resource_living_room_house_plant): the pot-and-saucer assembly, standing on a scale, gains 150-250 g (150-250 mL of water) between the pre-watering reading and a reading 60 s after pouring stops, and no more than 30 mL stands in the saucer. no_water_outside_saucer means no water on the floor, furniture, or route outside the pot and saucer. THOR mapping: watered <-> HousePlant isFilledWithLiquid=true (fillLiquid=water); switched_off(thor_object_kitchen_faucet_1) <-> Faucet isToggled=false; at(thor_object_watering_can_1, thor_resource_watering_can_home_spot) is an Atlas location predicate with no THOR state. THOR fills the WateringCan (isFilledWithLiquid) but has no pour action, and HousePlant isFilledWithLiquid can be set without the can ever tilting over the plant, so a simulated goal check cannot show that the can delivered the water. Intent: no plant-care intent exists in the seeds; intent_transport is kept because the task's defining difficulty is carrying a filled can between rooms and delivering its contents at a destination. A future intent_tend_plant may be proposed; see the task_suitability claim scope. HousePlant exists in the asset database but is not a part-A primary object, so it is a planning resource.

tasks.name_en: Switch off the living-room television so its screen goes dark
tasks.name_ja: リビングのテレビの電源を切り、画面を消す
instruction_variants: Turn off the TV in the living room.
Switch the television off so the screen is dark; you can use its power button or the remote.
リビングのテレビの電源を切ってください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the television is switched off; a reviewer sees a dark screen with no picture or backlight (a standby LED may remain lit). Labelled atomic: one object and one state change; locating and pressing the control are skills, not goals. THOR mapping: switched_on(tv) <-> isToggled=true initially, switched_off(tv) <-> isToggled=false at the end. THOR toggles the Television object directly; a real set is switched with its power button or a remote, so the control is a planning resource.

tasks.name_en: Switch on the floor lamp beside the sofa so it lights the room
tasks.name_ja: ソファ横のフロアランプを点けて部屋を明るくする
instruction_variants: Turn on the floor lamp next to the sofa.
Switch the standing lamp on without knocking it over.
ソファの横にあるフロアランプを点けてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the floor lamp is switched on; a reviewer sees its on/off indicator read on. Power policy (same as the desk lamp and house-light tasks): the lamp is unplugged and fitted with a battery dummy indicator wired to its own switch, or the task runs in simulation only; mains power is never used, and the indicator stands in for the bulb's light. Labelled atomic: one object and one state change; standing(lamp) is a preserved constraint, not a second goal. THOR mapping: switched_off(lamp) <-> isToggled=false initially, switched_on(lamp) <-> isToggled=true at the end. The asset does not say whether the lamp uses a pull chain, a rotary stem switch, or a foot switch; the setup records which one is used.

tasks.name_en: Lower the living-room window blinds to the sill so the window is covered
tasks.name_ja: リビングの窓のブラインドを窓台まで下ろして窓を覆う
instruction_variants: Lower the blinds on the living-room window all the way to the sill.
Bring the blinds down so the whole window is covered.
リビングの窓のブラインドを窓台まで下ろしてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the blinds are closed, defined as lowered to the sill across the full window width. Slat tilt is out of scope: on real blinds it is a separate control (tilt wand) from lowering (lift cord or cordless rail), and THOR has only one isOpen boolean, so the slats stay at the tilt recorded at setup. Labelled atomic: one fixture, one control, one state change. THOR mapping, unresolved: the brief maps closed(blinds) <-> isOpen=false, but the asset database gives Blinds_1 a 0.20 m tall default box and a 1.47 m tall 'open' box, so THOR's isOpen=true may be the lowered, window-covering pose. The planning condition thor_blinds_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator and the asset_compatibility limitation carry this; the Atlas goal is the physical observation above.

tasks.name_en: Put out the candle on the coffee table and leave it standing there (LED flame surrogate)
tasks.name_ja: ローテーブルのキャンドルを消して、そのまま立てておく（LEDの炎代替品）
instruction_variants: Put out the candle on the coffee table.
Turn off the candle and stand it back on the table where it was.
ローテーブルの上のキャンドルを消してください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the candle is extinguished and still stands on the coffee table; a reviewer sees no light from the flame tip. Labelled atomic: one object and one state change; the table position and upright pose are preserved constraints. THOR mapping: lit(candle) <-> isToggled=true initially, extinguished(candle) <-> isToggled=false at the end. No open flame at collection: an LED candle surrogate stands in for the flame. The surrogate's switch is usually on its base, so the recorded motion (lift, tip, switch) differs from snuffing or blowing out a real flame; the data captures the end state, not real flame handling.

tasks.name_en: Close the open laptop on the sofa and lay it flat on the coffee table
tasks.name_ja: ソファの上で開いているノートパソコンを閉じ、ローテーブルに平らに置く
instruction_variants: Close the laptop on the sofa and put it on the coffee table.
Shut the laptop that's open on the couch and lay it flat on the table.
ソファで開いたままのノートパソコンを閉じて、ローテーブルに置いてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the laptop is closed and lies flat on the coffee table; a reviewer sees the lid flush with the base and the whole laptop on the table top. Labelled compound: two goal predicates (closure and destination) on one object in one sitting. THOR mapping: open(laptop) <-> isOpen=true initially, closed(laptop) <-> isOpen=false at the end; on_top_of(laptop, coffee_table) <-> the laptop's parentReceptacles include the CoffeeTable. The laptop's isToggled state is not part of the goal.

tasks.name_en: Turn off the running shower so no water flows from the shower head
tasks.name_ja: 出ているシャワーを止めて、シャワーヘッドから水が出ない状態にする
instruction_variants: Turn off the shower.
Shut the shower valve so the water stops.
シャワーの水を止めてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the shower is switched off; a reviewer sees no water leaving the shower head (after the last drips) and the valve handle at its off mark. Labelled atomic: one fixture and one state change. THOR mapping: switched_on(shower) <-> ShowerHead isToggled=true initially, switched_off(shower) <-> isToggled=false at the end. THOR toggles the shower head itself; a real shower is shut at a separate wall valve, which is the planning control resource.

tasks.name_en: Draw the shower curtain closed along the full length of the tub
tasks.name_ja: シャワーカーテンを浴槽の端から端まで引いて閉じる
instruction_variants: Close the shower curtain.
Pull the curtain all the way across the bathtub.
シャワーカーテンを浴槽の端まで閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the shower curtain is drawn closed; a reviewer sees the curtain spread along the rod from wall to wall, covering the tub opening. Labelled atomic: one fixture and one state change. THOR mapping, unresolved: the brief maps closed(curtain) <-> isOpen=false, but the asset database gives Shower_Curtain_1 a 0.43 m wide default box and a 2.17 m wide 'open' box, so THOR's isOpen=true may be the spread, tub-covering pose (plain-language 'closed'). The planning condition thor_shower_curtain_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator and the asset_compatibility limitation carry this; the Atlas goal is the physical observation above.

tasks.name_en: Lower the raised toilet lid until it rests closed on the seat
tasks.name_ja: 上がっているトイレのふたを下ろし、便座の上に閉じる
instruction_variants: Close the toilet lid.
Put the toilet lid down gently so it rests on the seat.
トイレのふたを静かに閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Goal: the toilet lid is closed; a reviewer sees the lid resting flat on the seat with the bowl covered. Labelled atomic: one fixture and one state change; seat_down is a start condition, not a goal. THOR mapping: open(toilet) <-> isOpen=true initially, closed(toilet) <-> isOpen=false at the end; the database's taller 'open' box (1.19 m vs 1.04 m) is consistent with a raised lid. THOR models one openable part, while a real toilet has a separate seat and lid; this task moves only the lid.

tasks.name_en: Switch off the bedroom desk lamp
tasks.name_ja: 寝室のデスクランプを消す
instruction_variants: Switch off the desk lamp.
Turn the lamp on the bedroom desk off without moving it.
寝室の机の上のデスクランプを消してください。
tasks.notes: Atomic: one object, one device-state change (switched_off), one reach-and-press sequence. upright is a preserved condition, not a second goal. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on/switched_off = isToggled true/false on DeskLamp. Real collection uses an unplugged lamp with a battery indicator or a dummy switch panel, or runs in simulation only; the lamp bulb is never energised from mains during collection.

tasks.name_en: Make the unmade bed: duvet pulled up flat and pillow at the head end
tasks.name_ja: 乱れたベッドを整える（掛け布団を平らに引き上げ、枕を頭側に置く）
instruction_variants: Make the bed: pull the duvet up so it lies flat over the mattress and put the pillow at the head end.
Straighten the bunched duvet over the whole bed and move the pillow back to the headboard.
掛け布団をベッド全体に平らに引き上げ、枕を頭側に戻してベッドを整えてください。
tasks.notes: Compound, not atomic: THOR collapses bed-making into one flag, but the observable end state has several predicates over two objects (duvet covers the mattress and is smooth; pillow is on the bed at the head end). made() is not a separate goal: it is the conjunction of the goal predicates, and the THOR mapping made <-> Bed isDirty=false (unmade <-> isDirty=true; THOR uses isDirty for an unmade bed, not for soiling) is kept only for simulated checks. Default tolerances: smooth means no fold or bunch higher than 3 cm on the top surface; covers means the duvet covers the whole mattress top with left and right overhang within 10 cm of each other; the duvet's top edge lies within 15 cm of the pillow's foot-side edge. covers, smooth, and at_head_end have no THOR state and must be judged from images. Real collection needs real bedding; the THOR bed has no cloth simulation.

tasks.name_en: Put the keychain and the card inside the bedroom safe and close the safe door
tasks.name_ja: キーホルダーとカードを寝室の金庫に入れて扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Put the keychain and the card in the safe and shut the safe door.
Move the keys and the plastic card from the dresser top into the open safe, then close it.
キーホルダーとカードを金庫の中に入れて、金庫の扉を閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: two items stored and one closure, three goal predicates in one sitting at one place. The flat card is a hard grasp from a table top. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: inside(x, safe) = x's parentReceptacles contains the Safe; open/closed = isOpen true/false on Safe, so the goal is closed(thor_object_safe_18_1); thor_resource_safe_door is only the grasp handle used to swing the door shut and carries no state. THOR has no lock state, so locking is out of scope and the goal is door closed, not locked. Real collection uses a dummy key ring and a blank non-payment card, the safe is left unlocked with no code set, and nothing of value is stored.

tasks.name_en: Put the folded cloth in the top dresser drawer and close the drawer
tasks.name_ja: たたんだ布を整理だんすの一番上の引き出しにしまって閉める
instruction_variants: Put the folded cloth in the top dresser drawer and close it.
Open the dresser's top drawer, lay the folded cloth inside without unfolding it, and push the drawer shut.
たたんだ布を崩さずに整理だんすの一番上の引き出しに入れ、引き出しを閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (inside, with the cloth kept folded) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (open the drawer, then close it again), over two objects at one place. folded and closed hold at both start and end, so they are preserved end-state constraints, not goal changes. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: open/closed = isOpen on the child Drawer object of the dresser; inside = the Cloth's parentReceptacles contains that Drawer; folded has no THOR state (Cloth is rigid in THOR) and is judged by the cloth's footprint staying within its folded outline. The drawer is a planning resource because THOR drawers are room or furniture parts, not asset-database entries.

tasks.name_en: Clear the bedroom desk for the night: laptop closed, pen and pencil in the mug, desk lamp off
tasks.name_ja: 夜に寝室の机を片付ける（ノートPCを閉じ、ペンと鉛筆をマグに入れ、デスクランプを消す）
instruction_variants: Clear the desk for the night: close the laptop, put the pen and pencil in the mug, and switch off the desk lamp.
Shut the laptop lid, drop both writing tools into the mug, then turn the lamp off last.
ノートパソコンを閉じ、ペンと鉛筆をマグカップに入れてから、最後にデスクランプを消してください。
tasks.notes: Compound rather than workflow: four goal predicates over four objects, but all at one desk in one sitting with no reset or checkpoint between stages and one destination (the mug), so the rubric's workflow signs do not apply. The lamp is switched off last so the desk stays lit while working. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: open/closed = isOpen on Laptop; inside(x, mug) = x's parentReceptacles contains the Mug; switched_on/off = isToggled on DeskLamp. The desk lamp reuses thor_object_desk_lamp_1 from the atomic lamp task. Real collection uses an unplugged or retired laptop and an unplugged lamp.

tasks.name_en: Load the dirty cloths into the washing machine, close the door, and switch it on
tasks.name_ja: 汚れた布を洗濯機に入れ、扉を閉めて電源を入れる
instruction_variants: Put the two dirty cloths in the washing machine, close the door, and switch the machine on.
Load the cloths from the basket into the drum, shut the door, then press the power button.
かごの中の汚れた布2枚を洗濯機に入れ、扉を閉めてから電源を入れてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: load two deformable items, close the door, switch on; three goal predicates at one appliance in one sitting. switched_on is the goal state, not a wash cycle, so the task ends when the power indicator reads on. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: dirty = isDirty on Cloth; inside = parentReceptacles contains WashingMachine; open/closed = isOpen and switched_on/off = isToggled on WashingMachine, so the goal is closed(thor_object_washing_machine_1); thor_resource_washing_machine_door is only the grasp handle and carries no state. ProcTHOR houses have no laundry room, so the machine is placed in the bathroom scene on purpose. Real collection uses an unplugged machine with a dummy power indicator, or runs in simulation only; no water supply is connected and no cycle runs.

tasks.name_en: Put the spray bottle back in the under-sink cabinet and close the cabinet door
tasks.name_ja: スプレーボトルを洗面台下の収納に戻して扉を閉める
instruction_variants: Put the spray bottle back under the sink and close the cabinet.
Open the cabinet below the basin, stand the spray bottle inside, and shut the door.
スプレーボトルを洗面台の下の収納に立てて戻し、扉を閉めてください。
tasks.notes: Compound: one net change (inside, with the bottle kept upright) plus a transient articulation that must be reversed (open the cabinet door, then close it again), over two objects in one sitting. closed holds at both start and end, so it is a preserved end-state constraint, not a goal change. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: open/closed = isOpen on the Cabinet room part; inside = the SprayBottle's parentReceptacles contains that Cabinet; upright has no THOR state and is judged from the bottle's axis. The under-sink cabinet is a room-layout part in THOR, not an asset-database entry, so it is a planning resource. Real collection uses a capped bottle filled with water or empty, never a cleaning chemical.

tasks.name_en: Switch off the desk lamp and the bedroom, kitchen, and living-room lights before leaving
tasks.name_ja: 出かける前にデスクランプと寝室・キッチン・リビングの照明を消す
instruction_variants: Before leaving, turn off the desk lamp, then the bedroom, kitchen, and living-room lights.
Go room by room and switch off these four lights: the desk lamp and the bedroom, kitchen, and living-room lights.
出かける前に、デスクランプ、寝室、キッチン、リビングの順に4つの照明を消してください。
tasks.notes: Workflow: four device-state goals at four destinations in three rooms, with a checkpoint in each room before moving on. Scope is exactly these four lights, not every light in the house. Order matters only for safety (desk lamp before the bedroom ceiling light so the robot is not left in the dark). The robot's position is not part of the goal state; the proposed procedure optionally ends at the living-room switch by the front door, and the robot's start room is set in setup. Atlas-to-THOR mapping: switched_on/off = isToggled on LightSwitch (room lights) and on DeskLamp. Light_Switch_12 is the living-room switch; ProcTHOR may place the same switch asset in several rooms, so the other switches are planning resources. The desk lamp reuses thor_object_desk_lamp_1; its switched_off goal also appears in task_thor_r1_desk_lamp_switch_off (lamp alone) and task_thor_r1_desk_clear_for_night (one desk), which have different scopes. Real collection uses dummy switch panels and an unplugged lamp with a dummy indicator that stands in for each light, or runs in simulation only; the robot must navigate with house lights going off, so a navigation aid (robot light or depth sensing) is required.

requirements.reason: Countertop microwave with a clear work zone beside it.
Primary THOR asset; a physical microwave or articulated door source is needed for real collection.
The THOR mug asset used as the load item.
Counter area where the mug starts.
Opening and closing the hinged microwave door.
Grasping, lifting, and placing the mug on the turntable.
Safety: the heat source cannot be started; physical collection uses an unplugged unit.
No liquid is loaded, so nothing spills or heats.
Safety: a ceramic mug can break; use a padded counter or a declared unbreakable surrogate.

Approach the microwave front.
Pull the door open fully.
Grasp the mug by its handle or body.
Lift the mug from the counter.
Place the mug upright near the centre of the turntable.
Release the mug and withdraw the gripper from the cavity.
Push the door closed until it latches.

steps.description: Locate the mug and the microwave.
Grasp the mug.
Lift the mug.
Set the mug on the counter directly in front of the microwave.
Release the mug.
Open the microwave door with the freed gripper.
Re-grasp the staged mug.
Place it upright inside on the turntable.
Release and withdraw.
Close the door until it latches.
Verify the goal state.

requirements.reason: Room on the counter to stage the mug while the door is opened.

The door is latched closed.
The microwave is off (unplugged unit, or isToggled=false in simulation).

Place the empty mug upright on the counter work zone within reach.

Confirm the door latch engaged rather than resting against the mug.

requirements.reason: Toaster on a counter with a plate beside it.
Primary THOR asset; a physical toaster or mock toaster is needed for real collection.
One bread slice or foam slice surrogate sized to the slot.
Plate the slice starts on.
Holding the slice edge-on and pressing the lever.
A real slice bends and tears if pinched or forced into the slot.
Confirming the slice is fully seated below the slot rim.
Safety: no heating element is energised; physical collection uses an unplugged unit.
The setup states whether the unplugged surrogate's lever can latch; if not, the task is simulation-only.
Safety and repeatability: the slot is emptied before each episode.

Grasp the slice by its top crust edge.
Lift the slice and turn it upright.
Align the slice's lower edge with one slot opening.
Lower the slice into the slot until it rests on the carriage.
Release the slice.
Press the carriage lever down until it latches.
Verify the slice sits below the rim and the lever is latched (or isToggled=true).

The lever is latched down (surrogate) or the toaster isToggled=true (simulation).
The toaster is still upright and in place on the counter.

Declare whether the lever latches unpowered; if it does not, run the task in simulation only.

Confirm the toaster was not dragged or tipped when the lever was pressed.

Toaster slides when the lever is pressed

requirements.reason: Sink with faucet and adjacent counter.
Primary THOR asset; a real faucet or articulated faucet source is needed for physical collection.
Drinking cup with a marked fill band.
Basin under the spout; catches overflow.
Where the cup starts and ends.
Water flows into the cup and must stop within the fill band.
Holding and carrying the cup upright.
Reading the water level against the fill band.
Safety: running water near a powered robot is contained, or flow is disabled for a dry run.
Safety: the arm and wrist electronics near the spout are rated or covered for splashes.
Safety: a glass cup can break in the basin; a plastic cup is preferred.

procedures.label: Set cup in basin, toggle, retrieve

steps.description: Locate the cup, the spout, and the faucet control.
Grasp the cup.
Lift the cup to the sink.
Place the cup upright in the basin directly under the spout.
Release the cup.
Turn the faucet on.
Checkpoint: watch the water level reach the fill band.
Turn the faucet off.
Grasp the filled cup.
Lift it out of the basin, keeping it level.
Place it upright on the counter work zone.
Release the cup.
Verify the level is within the band, the faucet is off, and no water drips from the spout.

requirements.reason: The cup can stand in the basin while the robot operates the faucet.

steps.description: Locate the cup and faucet.
Grasp the cup.
Hold the cup under the spout.
Turn the faucet on with the second arm or the free hand.
Checkpoint: stop at the fill band.
Turn the faucet off.
Carry and place the cup on the counter.
Release.
Verify the goal state.

requirements.reason: One effector holds the cup while the other operates the faucet.

success_criteria: The water level in the cup lies between the marked minimum and maximum lines.

draft_notes: thor_round1: 24 tasks on 24 AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets (10 atomic, 11 compound, 3 workflow) across kitchen, living room, bedroom, bathroom, and a multi-room house, drafted by three claude-opus-5-5 subagents and merged. The lamp-off template from part C was folded into template_thor_switch_device_off.

thor_round1 part A: eight kitchen-appliance, water, and multi-room tasks anchored to AI2-THOR / ProcTHOR assets (Microwave_1, Toaster_1, Kitchen_Faucet_1, Pot_1, Bread_1, Paper_Towel_1, Mug_1, Watering_Can_1), drafted from data/research/thor_candidates.json.

Scenes (scene_home_living_room, scene_home_bedroom, scene_multi_room_house) and evidence (evidence_thor_task_design_round1, evidence_procthor_asset_database) are defined in the skeleton data/drafts/thor_round1.json and are not redefined here; no per-object evidence records are created.

Asset IDs, objectTypes, and state flags were checked against the asset database at commit d4c4c6a9fdd9679c8b9343d771c510016cd310df on 2026-09-25; the flags in object notes are each asset's own primaryProperty and secondaryProperties.

Resource IDs beginning thor_resource_ are planning object requirements, not ObjectInstances. Cabinet, StoveBurner, and StoveKnob are iTHOR room-prefab parts; Cup, GarbageCan, HousePlant, CoffeeTable, and Knife are asset-database types that are not primary objects of a part-A task. Tasks 1, 4, 7, and 8 bind the THOR mug or faucet ObjectInstances declared here.
Every task note maps its Atlas predicates to AI2-THOR state names (isOpen, isToggled, isDirty, isFilledWithLiquid, isSliced, isUsedUp, parentReceptacles).

Heat, knife, and water safety: the microwave, toaster, and stove stay unpowered or simulated; slicing is simulation-only or uses a pre-scored surrogate with a blunt tool; running water tasks declare a splash guard or dry run and splash-protected electronics.

New Atlas concepts proposed: object_kitchen_appliance (microwave, toaster), object_home_fixture (faucet), object_food_item (bread). Other objects reuse object_cookware, object_paper_item, object_drinkware, and object_liquid_container. Parts B and C may propose the same concept IDs; they are strings, not records, so no merge conflict arises.
Eight new templates (template_thor_*); no existing template carried the needed device-state goals.
The watering-can task keeps intent_transport because no plant-care intent exists; the reason is stated in its task_suitability claim scope, and a future intent_tend_plant may replace it.

Part B of thor_round1 (8 tasks): living-room television, floor lamp, window blinds, candle, and laptop; bathroom shower, shower curtain, and toilet lid. Built on the skeleton data/drafts/thor_round1.json; scenes, evidence_thor_task_design_round1, and evidence_procthor_asset_database are defined there and not redefined here.
Object IDs carry the THOR asset number (thor_object_television_1 etc.) so they cannot collide with other THOR assets of the same objectType drafted in parts A or C.

Resource IDs beginning thor_resource_ are planning object requirements (controls, sofa, coffee table, window, rod, bathtub, surrogates), not cataloged ObjectInstances or claims that matching assets exist.

Proposed new Atlas concepts used: object_lamp (floor lamp), object_decor (candle), object_home_fixture (blinds, shower head, shower curtain, toilet). Television and laptop reuse object_electronic_device.

Five new templates: template_thor_switch_device_off (television, shower), template_thor_switch_device_on (floor lamp), template_thor_close_openable_fixture (blinds, shower curtain, toilet lid), template_thor_extinguish_candle, template_thor_close_laptop_and_set_down.

For Blinds_1 and Shower_Curtain_1 the asset database's 'open' bounding box is the extended, covering pose, so THOR isOpen=true may mean plain-language 'closed'. Task goals follow the physical observation; the planning conditions thor_blinds_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator and thor_shower_curtain_isopen_pose_confirmed_in_simulator and both asset_compatibility limitations require the mapping to be confirmed in the simulator before goals are checked against isOpen.

THOR toggles state on the object itself (Television, FloorLamp, ShowerHead, Candle); real collection uses the physical control (power button or remote, lamp switch, wall valve, LED surrogate switch), listed as planning resources. The candle uses an LED surrogate and no open flame.

Part C of thor_round1 (8 tasks: desk lamp, bed, safe, dresser, desk, washing machine, spray bottle, light switches). Merges into data/drafts/thor_round1.json, which defines scene_home_living_room, scene_home_bedroom, scene_multi_room_house, evidence_thor_task_design_round1, and evidence_procthor_asset_database; they are not redefined here. scene_home_bathroom comes from gso_round1.

Only the primary asset of each task is an ObjectInstance (thor_object_<asset slug>, e.g. thor_object_desk_lamp_1) to avoid collisions with parts A and B. The desk lamp object is reused as a bound item in the desk and whole-house tasks.

Supporting items (keychain, card, cloths, duvet, pillow, pen, pencil, mug, laptop, drawers, cabinet and machine doors, under-sink cabinet, other light switches, rooms) are thor_resource_* planning object requirements, not ObjectInstances or claims that matching assets exist.

Catalog identity claims cite the shared evidence_procthor_asset_database; no per-object evidence is created. Every task_suitability claim cites evidence_thor_task_design_round1; other task claims stay unknown with no sources.

Granularity: 1 atomic (desk lamp), 6 compound, 1 workflow (whole-house lights). The bed task is compound because the observable made-bed end state has several predicates over the duvet and pillow, even though THOR models it as one isDirty flag. The desk task is compound, not workflow: one desk, one sitting, no reset or checkpoint stages, one destination.

The washing machine sits in scene_home_bathroom on purpose: ProcTHOR houses have no laundry room. Lamp power policy for the whole bundle: the desk lamp, floor lamp, washing machine, and light switches are unplugged with a dummy indicator, or simulation-only; each success criterion says the indicator stands in for the light or the cycle.

New Atlas concepts: object_lamp, object_furniture, object_household_appliance, object_home_fixture (as proposed in thor_candidates.json). The safe reuses object_receptacle and the spray bottle reuses object_cleaning_bottle.
Eight new templates (template_thor_*); none of the existing templates carried the device-state or articulated-closure goals needed.

Review response (thor_round1 review): compound notes now count one net change plus a transient articulation rather than preserved predicates; safe and washing-machine goals use closed() on the THOR object; the blinds task is scoped to lowering to the sill; the bed goal drops made() and carries numeric tolerances; the house-lights goal no longer includes robot position.
Activated 2026-09-25 after an independent Claude review (data/reviews/thor_round1.md) with all findings addressed; the Codex cross-lane review is still pending.
